method: Tiny actual stock TimeSeries v11 same binary. INSERT SELECT uses reinterpretAsFloat64(toUInt64(0x7ff0000000000002)) stale marker and a repeated identical timestamp with values1.0 and7.0; OPTIMIZE FINAL done. Native prometheusQueryRange avg by(stage)(avg_over_time(metric[1h])) compared with direct read from physical inner SAMPLES, old raw avg and corrected avgIf using exact stale UInt64 payload. No performance claim or C++ patch.

code_evidence.note: Range selectors remove ONLY exact stale marker reinterpretAsUInt64(value)==0x7ff0000000000002 and preserve ordinary NaN
Sort duplicate timestamp values; larger finite wins, NaN loses
Duplicate arbitration associative/commutative max finite; all-NaN may remain NaN

decision: PROVEN counterexample to candidate's general PromQL correctness: unmodified SQL avg on physical SAMPLES with stale payload gives NaN while native returns 5.0. An exact bit-filtered avgIf fixes this specific case. Duplicate timestamp 1,7 was reduced to maximum7 in stored SAMPLES, then avg(7,3)=5.0 matches native. This does not refute finite-sample R01 ABBA results.
limitations: Only one stale-plus-real and one within-row duplicate pair; no ordinary NaN preservation test, stale-only series, cross-insert duplicates, resets, histograms, regex, many native grid points or ACL.
Raw query speed not measured; adding bit filter may reduce 2x speedup and must be benchmarked again after an eligibility/correctness proof.
A stale marker must not be filtered by general isNaN; ordinary NaN is retained by native range selectors.
next_gate: Guard SQL fastpath by exact stale NaN bits before AVG; prove source-faithful duplicate arbitration across merge/backfill and ordinary NaN handling, then benchmark cost and exact multi-eval grid parity before considering C++ conditional rewrite.
